flags.observed_value: leakage_status="clean" on EVERY served insight_unit row for chart 482012f1 (15 of 30 rows inspected: retrodiction rows with T-90d cutoffs AND verdict_object rows AND load_bearing rows all read "clean" identically)
flags.reasoning: grep confirms the string "clean" is written as a bare Python literal at every INSERT call site in mi_darshana.py — no variable, no conditional, no leakage detector of any kind computes this value. This is exactly the §N.7 item 4 / §N.8 defect class ("a flag that reads '0 leaks' or 'verified clean' with no code path that could ever produce a different value is not a clean result — it is an unimplemented check wearing a clean result's clothes"). It is especially serious because leakage_status specifically claims to certify NO train/test contamination on blind-retrodiction rows (T-90d cutoff insight_units, whose entire epistemic value depends on the cutoff genuinely excluding future information) — the one place where a leakage claim matters most is exactly where nothing checks it. Contrast with the sibling writer mi_adhilepa.py:163, which correctly emits the honest 'not_assessed' tier for the identical concept with an explicit code comment: "'clean' is reserved for when a real leakage detector exists and passes." mi_darshana violates the convention its own sibling module documents.
